vulgar.e: From Middle English vulgare, from Latin vulgāris, from volgus, vulgus (“mob; common folk”), from Proto-Indo-European *welH-.

vulnerable.e: From Late Latin vulnerābilis (“injurious, wounding”), from Latin vulnerō (“to wound”).
vulnerable.g: More or most likely to be exposed to the chance of being attacked or harmed, either physically or emotionally.

vulture.e: Borrowed into Middle English from Anglo-Norman vultur, from Old French voutoir, voutre, from Latin vultur, voltur.
vulture.g: Any of several carrion-eating birds of the families Accipitridae and Cathartidae.
